title: Finite-stalk subobjects cover torsion sheaves on a field
statement: Let K be a field, let p be the geometric point Spec(AlgebraicClosure K) -> Spec K, and let M be a locally torsion abelian sheaf on the small etale site of Spec K [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves, def-weil-pbc-torsion-etale-sheaf, def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks]. The supremum in Subobject M of all subobjects N whose p-stalk is finite is the top subobject M. This is a statement about the lattice of subobjects, without any choice of a diagram or assertion of a colimit universal property.

source.place: Proof, paragraph 4: finite stable subgroups; Stacks Project 04JQ and 03SA

proof.text: Use [lem-exc-abelian-sheaves-gmodules] with a separable closure inside AlgebraicClosure K to identify the sheaf and its specified algebraic-closure stalk with a discrete continuous Galois module. The torsion geometric-stalk criterion [lem-weil-pbc-torsion-sheaf-characterizations] (also proved directly in WeilConjectures.AlgebraicGeometry.Sites.EtaleTorsion) implies every element has finite additive order.

For an element m, its stabilizer is open by discreteness. The absolute Galois group is profinite by [lem-galois-aut-profinite]; [lem-exc-etale-open-subgroup-quotient-finite-discrete] shows the quotient by the stabilizer is finite. Its orbit, identified with this quotient, is therefore finite.

The subgroup generated by the finite orbit is stable under Galois action, since each group element permutes the orbit. It is a finitely generated torsion abelian group and hence finite (Mathlib AddCommGroup.finite_of_fg_isAddTorsion). It contains m.

Transport that subgroup inclusion through the inverse of the equivalence [lem-exc-abelian-sheaves-gmodules]. The resulting subobject has finite stalk and contains m on the stalk. Let S be the supremum of all finite-stalk subobjects. Every m factors through the stalk of S because its finite subobject lies below S. Thus the stalk of S.arrow is surjective. It is monic by exactness, so is an isomorphism of groups. The field stalk is conservative by the same equivalence and the forgetful functor for discrete representations. Hence S.arrow is an isomorphism and S = top.
